extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in geometric analysis / Ricci flow
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and records the precise definitions, hypotheses and conclusions of Perelman's no-local-collapsing theorems, related comparison lemmas, and the Cheeger-type compactness (Hamilton) convergence theorem as presented in a graduate-level textbook on Ricci flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: κ-noncollapsed at (x0,t0) on scale r (Definition 3.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let κ, r be positive constants and gij(t), 0 ≤ t < T, be a solution to the Ricci flow on an n-dimensional manifold M. The solution gij(t) is called κ-noncollapsed at (x0, t0) on the scale r if whenever |Rm|(x,t) ≤ r^{-2} for all x ∈ B_{t0}(x0,r) and t ∈ [t0 - r^{2}, t0], we have Vol_{t0}(B_{t0}(x0,r)) ≥ κ r^{n}. Here B_{t0}(x0,r) is the geodesic ball centered at x0 with respect to the metric gij(t0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the basic quantitative noncollapsing condition used throughout; the curvature bound is enforced on the parabolic/geometric neighborhood and the volume lower bound is measured at time t0 with metric gij(t0).

rubrics_metrics.name: No local collapsing theorem I (Theorem 3.3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given any initial metric g_{ij} on an n-dimensional compact manifold M, let g_{ij}(t) be the solution to the Ricci flow on [0,T) starting at g_{ij}. Then there exist positive constants κ and ρ0 (depending only on the initial metric and T) such that for any t0 ∈ [0,T) and any x0 ∈ M the solution is κ-noncollapsed at (x0,t0) on all scales less than ρ0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The theorem asserts a uniform (in space and up to time T) κ-noncollapsing at sufficiently small scales; the proof uses Perelman's reduced volume monotonicity and a contradiction argument (blow-up/rescaled reduced volume estimates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman's stronger no-local-collapsing variant (comment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perelman obtained a stronger version where the curvature bound assumption on the parabolic ball is replaced by a curvature bound on the geodesic ball B_{t0}(x0,r), via the monotonicity of the μ-functional (or the W-functional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This remark indicates that replacing parabolic curvature control by instantaneous (time t0) geometric curvature bounds is possible using the μ (or W) functional; it motivates the variant Theorem 3.3.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: No local collapsing theorem I′ (Theorem 3.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose M is a compact Riemannian manifold and g_{ij}(t), 0 < t < T, is a solution to the Ricci flow. Then there exists a positive constant κ depending only on the initial metric and T such that: for any (x0,t0) with 0 < r ≤ √T, if R(x,t0) ≤ r^{-2} for all x ∈ B_{t0}(x0,r), then Vol_{t0}(B_{t0}(x0,r)) ≥ κ r^{n}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a variant where only a scalar curvature bound on the geodesic ball at time t0 is assumed (rather than full Rm bounds over a parabolic region). The proof uses the μ-functional lower bound µ(g(0),τ) and an explicit test function with cut-off ζ to bound the W-functional and hence obtain a volume lower bound; κ is constructed from µ_0 and explicit constants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of µ (mu) / W-functional to bound volumes (from proof of Theorem 3.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define µ(g,τ) = inf_{(4πτ)^{-n/2} e^{-f} dV=1} W(g,f,τ) and µ_0 = inf_{0≤τ≤2T} µ(g(0),τ) > -∞. By choosing an explicit test function f supported in the geodesic ball and using the scalar curvature bound one obtains a lower bound for W(g(t0),f,r^{2}) and thereby a lower bound for Vol_{t0}(B_{t0}(x0,r)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The construction picks a smooth cut-off ζ depending on r, normalizes to get f, computes W and uses the scalar curvature bound and bounds on ζ to derive an explicit κ; this is how the scalar-curvature-only hypothesis is turned into a volume lower bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parabolic Laplacian comparison and distance derivative estimates (Lemma 3.4.1, Perelman)
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) Suppose Ric(·,t0) ≤ (n-1)K on B_{t0}(x0,r0). Then at t = t0 and outside B_{t0}(x0,r0), the distance function d(x,t)=d_t(x,x0) satisfies the differential inequality: (∂/∂t - Δ) d ≥ - (n-1)( (2/3) K r0 + r0^{-1} ). (ii) Suppose Ric(·,t0) ≤ (n-1)K on B_{t0}(x0,r0) and B_{t0}(x1,r0) for some x0,x1. Then at t=t0, ∂/∂t d_t(x0,x1) ≥ - 2(n-1)( (2/3) K r0 + r0^{-1} ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are parabolic analogues/generalizations of Laplacian comparison and Hamilton's integral Bonnet-Myers type estimate; they provide quantitative control of the time-derivative and Laplacian of distance under Ricci upper bounds on suitable balls and are used in maximum-principle arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: No local collapsing theorem II (Theorem 3.4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any A > 0 there exists κ = κ(A) > 0 with the following property: if g_{ij}(t) is a complete solution to the Ricci flow on [0,r_{0}^{2}] with bounded curvature and satisfying |Rm|(x,t) ≤ r_{0}^{-2} whenever y ∈ B_{0}(x0,r0) and t ∈ [0,r_{0}^{2}], and Vol_{0}(B_{0}(x0,r0)) ≥ A^{-1} r_{0}^{n}, then g_{ij}(t) is κ-noncollapsed on all scales less than r0 at every point (x,t) ∈ B_{0}(x0, A r_{0}) × [0,r_{0}^{2}].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a relative noncollapsing statement for complete solutions with bounded curvature, with the hypotheses being local curvature control on a parabolic region and a lower bound on the initial ball volume; proof follows the same reduced-volume monotonicity/contradiction strategy as in Theorem I but requires extra localization arguments and parabolic comparison estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name:
C^{
locfty} convergence of marked geodesic balls (Definition 4.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a notion of convergence for marked manifolds/balls allowing noncompact limits and coordinate changes; it is distinct from convergence of tensors on a fixed manifold because diffeomorphisms are allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hamilton Cheeger-type compactness / convergence theorem (Theorem 4.1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description:
Let (M_k,g_k,p_k) be a sequence of complete n-dimensional marked Riemannian manifolds and consider geodesic balls B(p_k,s_k) of radius s_k (0 < s_k ≤ ∞) with s_k → s (0 < s ≤ ∞). Suppose (a) for every r < s and every integer l ≥ 0 there exists a constant B_{l,r} such that |∇^{l} Rm(g_k)| ≤ B_{l,r} on B(p_k,r) for all sufficiently large k, and (b) there exists δ>0 with inj(M_k,p_k) ≥ δ for all k. Then a subsequence of (B(p_k,s_k), g_k, p_k) converges in C^{
locfty} to a marked geodesic ball (B(p_∞,s), g_∞, p_∞).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a localized version of Hamilton's compactness theorem allowing noncompact limits and removing global diameter/injectivity hypotheses; hypotheses require uniform local bounds on curvature and all derivatives and a uniform positive lower bound of injectivity radius at the basepoints. The proof constructs controlled coverings, coordinate charts and approximate isometries, then diagonalizes to obtain the limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled covering and ball-count bounds used in the compactness proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Given local curvature bounds and a uniform injectivity radius at the basepoint, one can construct a positive decreasing C^{1} function ρ(r) and (for each r<s) constants λ(r) and N(r) and k(r) so that for large k: (i) B(p_k,r) is covered by at most λ(r) disjoint balls B(x^{α}_{k}, ˜˜ρ_{α}^{k}) with controlled radii; (ii) each such ball meets at most N(r) other balls; (iii) the radii r^{α}_{k} are uniformly controlled and converge along subsequences. These combinatorial/quantitative coverings enable uniform coordinate charts and volume/injectivity control needed for convergence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These technical covering/count bounds (ρ, ˜ρ, ˜˜ρ, λ(r), N(r), k(r)) are explicit conditions used in the Step 1 selection of centers and in proving local finiteness, which then permit passing to subsequences and constructing coordinate charts with uniform metric derivative bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of approximate isometries between members of the sequence (Step 2 construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any r<s and any tolerances (ε1,ε2,...,εp), for sufficiently large k,l one can find a diffeomorphism F_{kl} from a neighborhood of B(p_k,r) into B(p_l,s_l) that is an (ε1,...,εp)-approximate isometry in the sense that the p-th covariant derivatives of the pullback metric are uniformly small: |∇^{p} (F_{kl}^* g_l - g_k)| < ε_p on the neighborhood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
The maps F_{kl} are constructed by averaging local coordinate identifications (using the previously built charts and partitions of unity) and provide the C^{
locfty} closeness needed to pass to the limit; the construction uses bounds on transition maps and center-of-mass averaging to control derivatives.
